R306.note: filepath.IsLocal correctly blocks absolute paths and .. traversal for the zip-slip sink; minor: explanation overstates IsLocal as also blocking symlink escapes (it is purely lexical), but the code fix itself is sound and legitimate entries are unaffected.

R307.note: Maps the accepted MIME types to a fixed safe extension instead of deriving it from the user-supplied filename, closing the dangerous-extension vector; legitimate png/jpeg uploads still pass the unchanged fileFilter.

R308.note: Adds the missing requireRole('admin') to match every sibling admin route exactly; minimal, correct fix.

R309.note: Allowlist is the right shape for a require()-based loader, but it hardcodes only two placeholder plugin names ('shown as examples') and the write-up openly admits the map needs populating - as shipped it silently narrows which real plugins under ./plugins can load.

R310.note: Adds a chained auth interceptor plus a scoped ownership query that returns NotFound for both missing and not-owned rows (good anti-enumeration); assumes ctx already carries 'user_id' from some unlisted upstream auth layer, which is a reasonable scope boundary for this single-file case.

R311.note: Rebuilds the command as a proper RESP array of length-prefixed bulk strings, the correct encoding for this raw-socket Redis sink; no other observable behavior change.

R312.note: Changes loop bound from i<=n to i<n, matching the stated contract exactly.

R313.note: Checks offset>capacity before length>capacity-offset, avoiding underflow and matching the stated contract (valid offset writes still work, oversized writes rejected, capacity still passed explicitly).

R314.note: Ownership check closes the cross-tenant data leak, but returns 403 Forbid for a wrong-owner invoice versus 404 NotFound for a missing one, directly contradicting the stated contract that unauthorized IDs must not reveal more than the not-found path - an undisclosed ID-existence oracle.

R315.note: Switches to ProcessBuilder array form and rejects a leading '-' (good), but the Windows branch still explicitly invokes cmd.exe /c with attacker-controlled data; verified live on JDK 26/Windows that a value containing an embedded double-quote breaks out of ProcessBuilder's quoting and executes an injected command through cmd.exe, so the vector is not actually closed on that branch.

R316.note: Allowlist of literal table names satisfies the contract's 'server-owned mapping' requirement in effect (only an exact-match literal reaches the query), bound params for accountId/status retained, default ledger preserved.

R317.note: Removes the shell entirely and adds an IP/hostname validator matching the parameter's own domain plus a '--' terminator against option injection; legitimate hosts unaffected.

R318.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms allowlist correctly replaces the unverified decode; fails closed on missing secret or bad signature.

R319.note: Confirmed by running mathjs locally that evaluateFormula's scope binding (compiled.evaluate(order) where order is the raw {total,tax} object, not {order: {...}}) throws 'Undefined symbol order' for every order.-prefixed expression, including the contract's own legitimate example 'order.total + order.tax' - malicious code execution is blocked, but the stated legitimate use case is silently broken entirely.

R320.note: Confirmed via live JDK 26/Windows test that jdk.lang.Process.allowAmbiguousCommands is read fresh per Process creation (not cached at class-init), so setting it false before pb.start() genuinely blocks the quote-breakout .bat injection the default allows; undisclosed side effect: it mutates a JVM-wide system property with no scoping or restore, affecting any other concurrent/unrelated Process launches in the same JVM.
